name: wal-recovery-correctness
targetProperty: After crash, replaying WAL frames from last checkpoint restores all committed transactions

S0.label: S0
S0.content: After crash, replaying WAL frames from last checkpoint restores all committed transactions. This is the fundamental crash-recovery guarantee of WAL-mode databases.
S0.formal: ∀ txn T. committed(T) ∧ crash() → after_recovery(): data(T) is visible

G1.label: G1
G1.content: WAL frames form a checksum chain - corruption is detected

G2.label: G2
G2.content: Recovery reads WAL and identifies last valid commit frame via checksum chain
G2.formal: recovery stops at first checksum mismatch, uses last_valid_frame

G3.label: G3
G3.content: Commit frames are marked with db_size > 0, non-commit frames are excluded from recovery

G4.label: G4
G4.content: frame_cache is populated only with frames up to last_valid_frame during recovery

G5.label: G5
G5.content: Page reads consult frame_cache first, falling back to DB file

G6.label: G6
G6.content: Committed transactions have all their frames written with final commit frame having db_size > 0

A1.label: A1
A1.content: We assume the underlying filesystem and hardware honor fsync semantics: after fsync returns successfully, the data is durably stored and will survive power loss. This is a standard assumption for database durability.
A1.formal: fsync(file) returns OK → data is durable on storage media

A2.label: A2
A2.content:
**CAVEAT: SyncMode::Normal**

In SyncMode::Normal, fsync is skipped on individual commits (pager.rs line 3682). This means:
- The last committed transaction before a crash MAY be lost (WAL frames written but not fsync'd)
- Recovery will still work correctly: frames without valid checksum chain or incomplete commit markers will be discarded
- This is a documented trade-off for performance

The property "all committed transactions are recoverable" still holds for transactions that completed their fsync. Only in-flight transactions at crash time may be lost in Normal mode.
